profile.name: TrialHub CTMS
profile.business_function: Clinical Trial Management System for study planning, site management, subject enrolment tracking and monitoring visits
profile.description: In-house Java EE monolith built in 2011. Manages ~120 active studies, investigator sites, enrolment milestones and monitoring visit reports. Supports inspection readiness for FDA/EMA audits.
profile.tech_stack: Java 7, EJB 3.0, JSF 1.2 + RichFaces, Hibernate 3, Apache Ant build, deployed as a single EAR (~180k lines of code)
profile.database: Oracle Database 11g R2 Enterprise, ~1.2 TB, heavy use of PL/SQL packages and Oracle-specific SQL
profile.hosting: On-premises Oracle WebLogic 10.3.6 cluster (4 nodes) on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6
profile.integrations: EDC system (SOAP web services), IRT/randomisation vendor (SFTP files), safety database (nightly batch ETL via Quartz jobs), SharePoint for TMF documents, LDAP authentication
profile.users: ~1,800 users: clinical operations staff, CRAs and site users in 25 countries
profile.data_classification: GCP records with pseudonymised subject data (GDPR special category data); 21 CFR Part 11 audit trails; 25-year retention for trial master file records
profile.pain_points: Release cycle is 6 months because the full EAR must be revalidated; WebLogic licence costs; Oracle 11g unsupported; Java 7 security findings; poor performance for sites in APAC
profile.constraints: Subject data for EU sites must stay in the EU; inspection-ready audit trail must be preserved through migration; 2 studies in database lock during Q1

summary.headline: Refactor TrialHub in about a year: first replatform the EAR to containers and managed Oracle on AWS, then strangle out site-management and monitoring services - validating each increment so releases drop from 6-monthly to monthly.
top_risks: Audit trail continuity during data migration
Full re-validation for every release persists

architecture.architecture_style: Java EE monolith (single EAR) on a WebLogic cluster with PL/SQL-heavy Oracle
architecture.summary: A 180k-line Java 7 / EJB 3.0 application with a JSF 1.2 UI, packaged as one EAR on a 4-node WebLogic 10.3.6 cluster and backed by a 1.2 TB Oracle 11g database with significant PL/SQL. Five integrations mix SOAP, SFTP, nightly Quartz ETL and LDAP. Because everything ships as one EAR, every release requires full re-validation, which drives the 6-month release cycle.

dimensions.label: Technology currency
dimensions.rationale: Runtime, app server, database and OS are all out of support.

dimensions.label: Modularity & coupling
dimensions.rationale: One 180k-LOC EAR; modules exist in code but deploy and validate together.

dimensions.label: Statelessness & scalability
dimensions.rationale: Clustered, but stateful JSF sessions and in-server batch jobs limit elasticity.

dimensions.label: Data portability
dimensions.rationale: 1.2 TB of Oracle with heavy PL/SQL; easiest path is managed Oracle, not an engine change.

dimensions.label: Integration complexity
dimensions.rationale: Five integrations across SOAP, SFTP, batch ETL, SharePoint and LDAP, several vendor-owned.

dimensions.label: Compliance & validation
dimensions.rationale: GCP-critical with Part 11 audit trails, GDPR special category data, EU residency and 25-year retention.
evidence: EU subject data must stay in the EU

dimensions.label: DevOps maturity
dimensions.rationale: Ant builds, no automated tests and a 6-month validated release cycle.

risks.title: Business logic locked in PL/SQL
risks.description: Core rules live in Oracle packages, so moving engines or extracting services can change validated behaviour.
risks.mitigation: Keep Oracle (managed) during replatform; extract services only behind characterisation tests.

risks.title: Audit trail continuity during data migration
risks.description: Inspection-ready audit trails must survive the migration complete and unaltered.
risks.mitigation: Validated migration with row counts and hash reconciliation of audit tables; QA review before go-live.

risks.title: Full re-validation for every release persists
risks.description: Without modular releases and automated tests, the cloud move alone will not shorten the 6-month cycle.
risks.mitigation: Adopt CSA, automate regression OQ, and validate extracted services independently.

risks.title: Container and Kubernetes skills gap
risks.description: The team knows WebLogic, not containers, EKS or IaC.
risks.mitigation: Pair with a partner for the first two waves; platform team owns golden pipelines.

risks.title: Disruption to studies in database lock
risks.description: Two studies lock their databases in Q1; cutover then would jeopardise submissions.
risks.mitigation: Schedule cutover after Q1 lock; freeze changes for locking studies.

risks.title: EU subject data leaving the EU
risks.description: A single US-hosted deployment would breach residency commitments for EU subjects.
risks.mitigation: Deploy in an EU region with region-restricting guardrails; document transfers in the DPIA.

risks.title: Oracle licensing on cloud
risks.description: Licence terms for Oracle on cloud can raise costs unexpectedly.
risks.mitigation: Use licence-included managed Oracle and right-size; plan a later move of new services to PostgreSQL.

risks.title: APAC site latency persists
risks.description: Moving the same server-rendered UI to one region keeps APAC slow.
risks.mitigation: Serve the new UI from a CDN and keep APIs chatty-free.

opportunities.title: Monthly instead of 6-monthly releases
opportunities.benefit: Independently validated services and automated OQ shrink the release cycle.

opportunities.title: Drop WebLogic licences
opportunities.benefit: Open-source Jakarta EE runtime on containers removes WebLogic licence cost.

opportunities.title: Faster experience for global sites
opportunities.benefit: A CDN-served UI improves performance in 25 countries.

opportunities.title: Inspection readiness on demand
opportunities.benefit: Centralised immutable audit logs make inspection evidence quick to produce.

opportunities.title: Self-service site onboarding
opportunities.benefit: Federated identity with MFA replaces manual site-user management.

plan.headline: Refactor TrialHub in about a year: first replatform the EAR to containers and managed Oracle on AWS, then strangle out site-management and monitoring services - validating each increment so releases drop from 6-monthly to monthly.

patterns.name: Strangler fig
patterns.why: Carve services out of the EAR one domain at a time, validating each small increment instead of the whole system.

patterns.name: Replatform to managed PaaS
patterns.why: Exit end-of-life WebLogic, Java 7 and Oracle 11g first while keeping PL/SQL logic intact.

patterns.name: API gateway facade
patterns.why: Decouples the EDC SOAP contract from EJBs and routes traffic between legacy and new services.

patterns.name: GxP landing zone
patterns.why: EU-resident, policy-guarded accounts with immutable audit logging for an inspected GCP system.

component_strategies.rationale: Replace JSF/RichFaces with a modern SPA served from a CDN for global sites, module by module.
Containerise the EAR on an open-source Jakarta EE runtime first, then extract site and monitoring services.
Licence-included managed Oracle keeps PL/SQL unchanged; new services get their own PostgreSQL schemas.
Move batch out of the app server into observable, retryable managed pipelines.
Vendor system stays; an API facade decouples its SOAP contract.
Vendor keeps SFTP; the endpoint moves to a managed service.
Out of scope; receives data from the new pipeline.
Federated identity with MFA for staff and external site users.
component_strategies.target_service: Amazon Cognito federated with corporate IdP

plan.target_summary: AWS in an EU region inside a GxP landing zone: a CDN-served SPA, the containerised core on Amazon EKS with extracted site and monitoring services, licence-included Amazon RDS for Oracle, an API Gateway facade for EDC, Transfer Family for IRT files, Step Functions/Glue for safety reconciliation, Cognito federation with MFA, and CloudTrail/CloudWatch for immutable audit logging.

target_components.name: TrialHub Web
target_components.description: SPA served close to global sites.

target_components.name: API Facade
target_components.description: Single entry for UI and EDC; routes legacy vs new.

target_components.name: Site & Monitoring Services
target_components.description: First services extracted via strangler fig.

target_components.name: Identity
target_components.description: SSO with MFA for staff and sites.

target_components.name: Audit & Monitoring
target_components.description: Immutable, retained audit and app logs.

roadmap.name: Mobilise and validation planning
objectives: Agree scope, strategy and validation approach
activities: GxP impact assessment and CSA-based validation plan
AWS supplier qualification and quality agreement
Map database-lock windows for active studies

roadmap.name: GxP landing zone
activities: Multi-account landing zone with region guardrails
EKS platform, CI/CD and IaC under change control
CloudTrail and CloudWatch audit logging

roadmap.name: Replatform the monolith
activities: Upgrade to a supported Java and an open-source Jakarta EE runtime
Containerise the EAR on EKS
Migrate Oracle 11g to RDS for Oracle with audit-table hash reconciliation
Automate the regression OQ suite

roadmap.name: Production cutover
activities: Cutover after Q1 database locks
Parallel run and PQ with clinical operations
Hypercare

roadmap.name: Strangle site and monitoring services
objectives: First independently validated services and new UI
activities: Extract site management and monitoring-visit services
New SPA modules for these domains
API Gateway routes legacy vs new

roadmap.name: Integration modernisation
activities: API facade for EDC SOAP
Transfer Family for IRT files
Step Functions and Glue for safety reconciliation

roadmap.name: Optimise and decommission
activities: Decommission WebLogic cluster and Oracle 11g
Archive per 25-year retention
Cost optimisation and periodic review

quick_wins: Start an automated regression suite on the current system - it is reused in every phase
Move the nightly safety ETL out of the EAR into a monitored scheduler
Inventory PL/SQL packages and tag those holding validated business rules
Agree the post-Q1 cutover window with the two locking studies
